final_prompt:
Please write a polite email to my landlord about the late fee. Cite the lease section. Thank you!

<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

**Subject:** Late fee on Unit 3B – Lease Section 4.2

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your message regarding the late fee on my account for this month. I understand the importance of on-time payments, and I want to make sure we're on the same page about the terms of our lease.

Rent was received on the 3rd of the month. Under Section 4.2 of the Maple Court residential lease, rent is due on the 1st, and a grace period applies through the 5th. The lease states that no late fees may be charged during the grace period. Since my payment arrived within that window, I don't believe the $75 late fee is applicable, and I'd appreciate it being removed from my account.

Please let me know once the adjustment has been made. If you have any questions or see it differently, I'm happy to discuss it.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Best regards,
[Your Name]
Unit 3B

---

If you'd like, I can also make the tone firmer or softer, or add a line asking for written confirmation of the credit.
